name: agent-builder-optional-release-agent
body:
The distributed `agent-builder` agent template `opencode-suite/agents/agent-builder.md` (product source embedded into the `apg` binary via `include_str!` and installed by `apg init` into `~/.opencode/agents/`) must be able to scaffold an OPTIONAL, per-repo `release-agent` — the slot the removed optional `coordinator` vacated. Unlike the distributed suite agents, the `release-agent` is GENERATED per repo, never distributed: it needs repo-specific release-artefact write grants (version files, formulae, changelog, …) and the repo's remote/branch conventions, interviewed per repo exactly like the build gates.

Its shape: `mode: subagent`, `hidden: true`, `generated: true`; no `question` (it routes questions through the coordinator); it never actions Feedback — it returns an ACTIONED/WONT-FIX claim like every generated agent. It is grant-unusual in exactly one way: it is the ONLY generated agent granted `git push *` and `git tag *`, and its grant is `ask` — every push/tag command prompts for explicit human approval. Every OTHER generated agent gets no push/tag grant at all (denied by deny-by-default).

The `release-agent` performs the repo's release: it is granted the release-adjacent git ops (tagging and pushing the branch and tags) plus write access to the repo's project-specific release artefacts. The `codebase-navigator` dispatches it through the `task` tool ONLY after obtaining **explicit user consent**, and the grant is `ask`, so approval surfaces both at dispatch and per command.

This is a deliberate CARVE-OUT of the repo's recurring "push/tag remain human-approved acts" rule (the scoped law is `requirements.constraint.push-tag-release-agent-carve-out`, restated by `requirements.requirement.push-tag-human-approved-release-only`): the rule continues to bind every other agent and path; only the deliberately-invoked release-agent is exempt, and only behind the consent gate and the per-op `ask`.

The carve-out is an AGENT-policy statement, NOT a binary one. The `apg` binary still never pushes or tags: it is git2-only (`default-features = false`; the git CLI is never shelled out to) and `scripts/release.sh` itself still never pushes — the release-agent may run it and then push/tag itself. The wording of that binary-policy statement on the binary-doc surfaces is corrected from "human acts" to "human-approved acts" by `requirements.requirement.push-tag-human-approved-release-only`; the binary's behaviour is unchanged.

Surfaces to edit (all real `docs` File nodes in the branch graph):
- `opencode-suite/agents/agent-builder.md` — add the optional `release-agent` to the generated set (the roster intro, a `### release-agent (optional)` section, the workflow interview bullet, and the step-4/step-5 scaffold) and its grant shape (push/tag `ask`, repo-specific release-artefact edits, interviewed); rewrite its push/tag prose (currently ~lines 90, 172-173, 289, 314-320, 376-378) to state that ONLY the release-agent is granted push/tag, as `ask`, and that every other generated agent gets no push/tag grant.
- `opencode-suite/agents/codebase-navigator.md` — state that the navigator obtains explicit user consent BEFORE tasking the release-agent; add `release-agent` to its `task` allowlist (currently lines 6-15); scope its push/tag clause (currently lines 460-461) to the human-approved phrasing.
- `AGENTS.md` — document the optional release-agent, the consent gate, and the release-agent-only push/tag rule, and correct the "human acts" phrasing (currently lines 107-108, 130-131, 795).

Acceptance criteria:
- `opencode-suite/agents/agent-builder.md` offers and scaffolds the optional per-repo `release-agent`: `mode: subagent`, `hidden: true`, `generated: true`, no `question`, returning ACTIONED/WONT-FIX claims; it is the ONLY generated agent granted push/tag, as `ask`; every other generated agent carries no push/tag grant; its release-artefact write grants are interviewed per repo.
- `opencode-suite/agents/codebase-navigator.md` states the navigator obtains explicit user consent BEFORE dispatching the release-agent, and its `task` allowlist contains `release-agent`.
- `AGENTS.md` documents the release-agent, the consent gate, the release-agent-only push/tag rule and the human-approved phrasing.
- The binary's git2-only behaviour is unchanged (it never pushes or tags and never shells out to the git CLI; `scripts/release.sh` still never pushes); the binary-doc phrasing correction is governed by `requirements.requirement.push-tag-human-approved-release-only`.
- Scope is product source + the repo guide only: `opencode-suite/agents/agent-builder.md`, `opencode-suite/agents/codebase-navigator.md`, `AGENTS.md`. The repo's own `.opencode/agents/**` are consumer artifacts and are NOT edited.
